summary: Self-hosted AI assistant you message from WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and more, with each agent sandboxed in its own Docker container.

heroCommands.command: git clone https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw.git && cd nanoclaw && bash nanoclaw.sh

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: NanoClaw is a lightweight personal assistant that runs AI agents in isolated containers and connects them to messaging apps. You chat with it from WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage, email and many other channels, and it can run scheduled tasks, search the web and work in folders you allow.
sixtySeconds.problem: Always-on AI assistants that can touch your files and accounts are risky to run loosely. NanoClaw keeps each agent in its own container with only the mounts you allow, and keeps API keys in a credential gateway rather than in the agent.
whoFor: People who want a personal assistant in their chat apps
Developers who want a small, readable codebase to customize
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for container isolation, many messaging channels and a codebase small enough to understand and change with your coding agent.
requirements: A model credential (Claude by default, or Codex, Cursor or OpenCode)

overview: The nanoclaw.sh script takes a fresh machine to a named agent you can message. It installs or updates Node and pnpm, installs Docker if missing, sets up a credential gateway, gets an agent image and pairs your first channel.
Each agent group has its own instructions file, memory and containers. You can give each channel its own agent or share one agent across channels. Agents can run one-off or recurring scheduled tasks.
NanoClaw works without an account. The free account and portal are optional, and the README lists exactly what is sent when you use them. It is MIT licensed.

steps.title: Run setup
steps.body: Run it directly in a terminal, not inside a coding agent session, because it needs interactive prompts.

steps.title: Pair a channel
steps.body: Follow the wizard to connect Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp or another app, or chat from the terminal.

firstRun.title: Name your assistant
firstRun.body: Setup asks for a name (default Nano).

firstRun.title: Send a message
firstRun.body: Message it directly or @mention its bot in a group chat.

costs.label: NanoClaw
costs.value: Free and open source under MIT. The optional account is free.

costs.label: Models
costs.value: Claude or your chosen runtime bills for usage.

troubleshooting.solution: Setup can hand the failure to Claude Code (or Codex/OpenCode) to diagnose, then retry from that step.

troubleshooting.problem: Setup acts oddly in an agent session
troubleshooting.solution: Run nanoclaw.sh directly in your terminal.
